entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5903"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 38</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.38.1-Ps.38.22">Psa 38:1-22</reference>. To bring to remembrance, or, remind God of His mercy and himself of his sin. Appealing to God for relief from His heavy chastisement, the Psalmist avows his integrity before men, complains of the defection of friends and persecution of enemies, and in a submissive spirit, casting himself on God, with penitent confession he pleads God's covenant relation and his innocence of the charges of his enemies, and prays for divine comfort and help.</title> <div sID="gen8976" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5903"/>1-4. He deprecates deserved punishment, which is described (<reference osisRef="Ps.6.1">Psa 6:1</reference>), under the figure of bodily disease [Psa 38:3]. <div eID="gen8976" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5915"/><div sID="gen8993" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5915"/>21-22. (Compare <reference osisRef="Ps.22.19">Psa 22:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.35.3">35:3</reference>). All terms of frequent use. In this Psalm the language is generally susceptible of application to Christ as a sufferer, David, as such, typifying Him. This does not require us to apply the confessions of sin, but only the pains or penalties which He bore for us. <chapter eID="Ps.38"/>
